observations.pairA_difference: A very subtle difference in the panel's edge/shadow treatment along its entire rounded border (top, both sides, bottom corners). In D6B1 the dark panel blends into the grey desktop with a soft, gradual falloff (a faint shadow/blur bleeding a few pixels into the background and slightly lightening the panel's own edge pixels). In 72E4 that same border transitions abruptly from panel-dark to background-grey with almost no blur, giving a crisper, harder edge. It is not visible at a casual glance; it only shows up on close inspection of the outline, most noticeably around the bottom corners and the thin vertical side edges.
observations.pairB_difference: The same type of difference as pair A, at the same relative position: A83F has a softer, more blurred edge/shadow around the panel's border, while 5C09 has a crisper, sharper-edged transition to the desktop grey. Interior content (text, icons, progress bar) is identical between the two.
observations.content_lost: no - all visible text and elements are present in both images of both pairs; the only difference is in the border/edge rendering, not in any content.

why.pairA: 72E4's crisp, nearly shadow-less edge reads as a flush cutout of the screen's own top edge, whereas D6B1's soft blurred edge is the classic elevation shadow cue of a floating window.
why.pairB: Same logic as pair A: 5C09's sharper border keeps the panel feeling attached to the screen edge, while A83F's softer blur makes it read more like a window hovering over the desktop.
